title: Where and when the Sam Morgan records were made
summary: The Sam Morgan records for Columbia were made in New Orleans, possibly 1926, and Brown heard he was the first recorded bass.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh, to go back to the Sam Morgan band, and you tell us when you made those records, was that in Chicago or where did you make those records, for Columbia? Yeah, we made those records out on Canal Street.
At Gotcha was Billing. Did you ever go to Chicago with the band?
Yeah. Yeah, we went to Chicago.
Oh, I forgot the year now. My, that was in 26. Wasn't that the year? Something along in about that time. Around 26, 25 or 26. When did you make the records, do you remember? Yeah. Yeah. Oh, no.
It was after that though, wasn't it? But I know, I can remember, they said, when, uh, when Will was up there making records, I
think it said, that was the first bass ever was on records. I had to hear, when I made the records with Sam Morgan. Yeah.
That's why you come through real good on those, you can really hear the bass. Yeah, did you hear? Yeah, sir.
Uh huh. Yeah, I, I don't know if I'm the person, but that's what I heard some fellow said, you know?
Well, before electric days, you couldn't hear the bass much on the record. No, you couldn't. Those were electric recording. Do you remember who else was in the band at that time on the records?
